title: Ship delay notifications for shipments
summary: Tell customers when their delivery will miss its promised time, before they have to ask.
deliverable: A tested notification in the shipment tracker
brief: Notify the customer when the carrier's latest estimate means a delivery will arrive more than 2 hours after the promised time.
questions:
Q1. What counts as late: any delay, or a margin?
Q2. Which estimate do we trust?
Q3. How many notifications per shipment?
Q4. Which time zone does the customer see?
answers:
Q1. More than 2 hours after the promised time.
Q2. The carrier's latest ETA, which arrives in UTC.
Q3. One notification per shipment, plus one more if the new estimate slips by a further 2 hours.
Q4. The delivery address's local time.
draftA:
REQ-1 Compare the carrier ETA with the promised delivery time; notify when the ETA is more than 2 hours later.
REQ-2 Promised times are stored as the customer saw them (local time); carrier ETAs are read as given.
AC-1 SHP-5120 promised 2026-11-12 18:00, carrier ETA 13:00: on time, no notification.
draftB:
REQ-1 Convert both times to UTC before comparing: promised 2026-11-12 18:00 India time is 12:30 UTC.
REQ-2 Notify when ETA minus promised time is more than 2 hours.
REQ-3 Show times to the customer in the delivery address's local time.
AC-1 SHP-5120: ETA 13:00 UTC (18:30 local) is 30 minutes late, no notification.
AC-2 SHP-5121: ETA 15:30 UTC (21:00 local) is 3 hours late, notify.
reviewOfA:
D-A1 · P0 · Time-zone error
  REQ-2 compares a local promised time with a UTC carrier ETA as if they were the same clock. For an India delivery, 13:00 UTC is 18:30 local, 30 minutes late, not 5 hours early as AC-1 implies. Depending on the zone this hides real delays or invents false ones.
D-A2 · P1 · Repeat notifications
  No rule for a second notification if the estimate slips further.
reviewOfB:
D-B1 · P1 · Daylight saving
  Zones with daylight saving need the offset for the delivery date, not today's.
Strengths: both times converted to UTC; both worked examples are correct.
synthesis:
Kept from B: compare in UTC, show in local time, both worked examples.
Kept from A: the 2-hour margin wording.
Fixed D-A1: all comparisons in UTC; promised times are stored with their zone.
Fixed D-A2 and D-B1: a second notice only after a further 2-hour slip; offsets use the delivery date.
Defects resolved: 3 of 3.

output:
## Approved requirements
- REQ-1 Every comparison is in UTC. Promised times are stored with their time zone; carrier ETAs arrive in UTC.
- REQ-2 Notify the customer when the ETA is more than 2 hours after the promised time.
- REQ-3 Send a second notice only if the ETA slips a further 2 hours beyond the ETA at the last notice.
- REQ-4 Show times in the delivery address's local time, using the offset for the delivery date (daylight saving).
- AC-1 SHP-5120 promised 2026-11-12 18:00 India time (12:30 UTC). ETA 13:00 UTC (18:30 local): 30 minutes late, no notice.
- AC-2 SHP-5121, same promise. ETA 15:30 UTC (21:00 local): 3 hours late, notify.
## What the customer now gets
- "Your delivery SHP-5121 is running late. New estimate: 12 Nov, 21:00 (India time). It was promised for 18:00. We'll tell you if it changes again."
## Evidence
- 7 tests passing, after the repeat-notice bug was fixed.
- Replay of last week's shipments: 214 notices, none for deliveries that arrived on time.

contrast.before: REQ-2 Promised times are stored as the customer saw them (local time); carrier ETAs are read as given.
contrast.after: REQ-1 Every comparison is in UTC. Promised times are stored with their time zone; carrier ETAs arrive in UTC.
contrast.why: India time and UTC were compared as if they were the same clock, a 5½-hour error: real delays would go unreported and on-time deliveries could trigger apologies.

architecture.draft:
Components:
- src/tracking/delay.ts: minutesLate(promisedAt, etaUtc).
- src/tracking/notify.ts: decides when to notify; one notice, then another after a further 2-hour slip.
- A carrier webhook that receives ETA updates.
- Messaging: SMS and email through the existing notification service.
Data: shipments gain promised_at with its time zone; a notices table records each notice and the ETA it was based on.
File fence: src/tracking/*, src/webhooks/carrierEta.ts, migrations/0031_promised_zone.sql and their tests.
architecture.review:
AR-1 · P1 · Out-of-order updates
  Carriers resend old ETAs. Ignore an update older than the last one received, or a stale ETA could trigger a notice.
AR-2 · P1 · Quiet hours
  A 03:00 text about a delay is worse than none. Hold notices between 21:00 and 08:00 local time.
Strengths: every time carries its zone; notices record the ETA they were based on.
architecture.final:
Kept: the delay rule, the notice rule and the notices table.
Fixed AR-1: each ETA update carries the carrier's timestamp; older updates are ignored.
Fixed AR-2: notices are held between 21:00 and 08:00 local time.
File fence: src/tracking/*, src/webhooks/carrierEta.ts, migrations/0031_promised_zone.sql and their tests.

codeReview.review:
CR-1 · P1 · Webhook not verified
  carrierEta.ts accepts any POST. Verify the carrier's signature header.
CR-2 · P2 · Duplicate time parsing
  delay.ts and notify.ts each parse ISO strings; share one helper.
CR-3 · P2 · Library
  Use a date library instead of Intl for time zones.
codeReview.revise:
CR-1 applied: a request without a valid signature gets 401.
CR-2 applied: one parse helper.
CR-3 declined: Intl handles the zones we need without a new dependency, and the daylight-saving test covers it.
